output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service - Aria 3 recalibration and repair

I promised Dana I would write this up after I had taken my machine through a real trial. It has now been back for eight days of civil trial work, so I feel I can give it a fair review.

I took my Stenvale Aria 3 to Harbor Point Steno Service in Towson on Monday, October 19, for a full recalibration, a number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and a firmware update. I picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days against the ten business days quoted. Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road, with free parking in back.

The original estimate was $285. Gloria found that the internal battery was holding about 60% of its rated capacity and emailed to ask whether I wanted it replaced for another $25. She did not proceed until I approved it. The final bill was $310, which I think was fair for the work done, and I appreciated being asked before anything was added. I paid for it myself, as I do all my equipment; the court did not reimburse me.

The invoice lists a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, a firmware update and the battery replacement. The work has a 90-day warranty. The machine also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before, and it is useful to have something specific to keep with my records.

Harbor Point offered me an Aria 2 loaner while mine was in the shop. It got me through the gap, but its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I let Gloria know; she said they would repair the arm before sending it out again.

The phone situation is the real weakness. The line is staffed only Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, which is not much help if you are working a Monday docket. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress; it rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day. I was satisfied with the eventual turnaround, but being unable to leave a message is a problem worth knowing about.

My first full day back on the Aria 3 was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight days of trial, I am pleased with how it is writing.

Dana, based on this experience, I would trust Gloria with your Aria. The repair has held up under the kind of work that showed the problem, and she was careful about getting approval for the extra charge. I would also plan around the limited phone hours and check the loaner’s tilt arm before taking it out.
